author: Bahá'u'lláh
note: Curated catalogue of IDEAS (not terms). `groups` = the claim-meaning groups (planning/merge-review/iqan-groups.json, built from the 3,523 proof-gated concept claims) that attest each idea; terms, original-script roots and exemplar paragraphs are derived from them. Sibling ideas marked `senseOf` are distinct authorized meanings of one symbol — never collapsed.

themes.title: Why every age rejects its Messenger

ideas.title: Denial recurs in every age
ideas.statement: In every Dispensation the people deny, mock and persecute the new Messenger, as their forebears did the one before.

ideas.title: The divines as the foremost opponents
ideas.statement: The religious leaders of each age, attached to leadership and learning, are the first to reject the Manifestation and lead the people astray.

ideas.title: The lowly recognize, the exalted are abased
ideas.statement: Obscure and unlearned souls often recognize the new Revelation while the learned and exalted reject it; the Day of God inverts rank.

ideas.title: Literal reading of scripture as a veil
ideas.statement: Clinging to the outward, literal sense of prophecy and tradition prevents recognition; the Word of God has inner meanings.

ideas.title: Corruption of scripture means perversion of meaning
ideas.statement: The corruption (taḥríf) of the Holy Books refers to the perversion of their meaning by the divines, not the alteration of the text.

ideas.title: Vain imaginings and idle fancy
ideas.statement: People measure the Revelation by their own fancies and imaginings, which confine them as in a cage and blind them to truth.

ideas.title: Heedlessness, the sleep of the soul
ideas.statement: Heedlessness is a spiritual sleep and remoteness in which the soul, though outwardly alive, is as one dead in the grave of self.

ideas.title: The accusations: sorcery, madness, infidelity
ideas.statement: The Manifestations are accused of sorcery, falsehood and infidelity and are met with proud disdain, as every Prophet was.

ideas.title: The sufferings of the Manifestations
ideas.statement: The Manifestations endure imprisonment, exile and cruelty at the hands of those they came to save; their patience is itself a sign.

ideas.title: Scripture speaks in symbols with inner meaning
ideas.statement: The words of the Prophets carry inner meanings veiled in symbolic language, understood only by pure hearts and not by outward learning.

ideas.title: Sun, moon and stars
ideas.statement: The sun, moon and stars signify the Manifestations and the divines and ordinances of a former Dispensation, whose light is darkened when a new Revelation appears.

ideas.title: Clouds as the veils that test the people
ideas.statement: The 'clouds' in which the Son of Man comes are the things contrary to people's desires — the Manifestation's human condition and the change of laws — which veil Him from the heedless.

ideas.title: Clouds of mercy and showers of grace
ideas.statement: The clouds are also the source of the rain of divine mercy and knowledge that revives the hearts.

ideas.title: Heaven as the realm of Revelation
ideas.statement: 'Heaven' signifies the heaven of divine Will and Revelation — the loftiness of the Manifestation's Cause — not the visible sky.

ideas.title: Earth as the hearts, changed into another earth
ideas.statement: 'Earth' signifies the earth of knowledge and of the hearts; its changing into another earth is the transformation of understanding by the new Revelation.

ideas.title: Resurrection and Judgement are spiritual
ideas.statement: The Day of Resurrection is the advent of the Manifestation; the dead are the heedless, and their raising is the quickening of faith.

ideas.title: The return of the Prophets
ideas.statement: The 'return' of past Prophets is the return of their reality and attributes in a new Manifestation, not the reappearance of the same person.

ideas.title: The trumpet-blast
ideas.statement: The trumpet is the call of the new Revelation, which awakens those dead in heedlessness.

ideas.title: The signs foretold of the Advent
ideas.statement: The signs foretold for the coming of a Manifestation — the star, the heralds, the tribulations — are fulfilled in their inner meaning and recur with every Revelation.

ideas.title: Bread, wine, waters and the Kawthar of knowledge
ideas.statement: Bread from heaven, the cup, the wine and the waters of Kawthar signify the spiritual sustenance of divine knowledge and nearness.

ideas.title: Fire: the burning Bush and the fire of self
ideas.statement: Fire signifies both the fire of divine love and wisdom in the sacred Tree, and the hellish fire of self, misbelief and passion.

ideas.title: The Bird of Heaven and its melody
ideas.statement: The mystic Bird and its melodies signify the Revelation's utterance and the soul's flight toward God.

ideas.title: Transmutation: copper into gold
ideas.statement: As the elixir turns copper into gold, the Word of God transforms souls in an instant — unbelief into faith, iniquity into righteousness.

ideas.title: The fatherless birth of Jesus
ideas.statement: The fatherless birth of Jesus was a test that the people of His day could not bear.

ideas.title: The Essence of God is unknowable
ideas.statement: The divine Essence is exalted beyond all knowing; no one can reach It, and all praise of It returns to the praiser.

ideas.title: The Manifestations as mirrors of God
ideas.statement: God has made His Manifestations the primal mirrors of His names and attributes; to know them is to know God.

ideas.title: Attaining the Presence of God
ideas.statement: The 'Presence of God' promised in scripture is attainment unto the presence of His Manifestation.

ideas.title: The unity of the Manifestations
ideas.statement: All the Manifestations are one in essence — one Name, one Cause, one Self — so each may truly claim to be the return of all.

ideas.title: The distinction of the Manifestations
ideas.statement: In their human condition and mission the Manifestations differ in degree, law and intensity of Revelation, while one in essence.

ideas.title: The Seal of the Prophets, the Beginning and the End
ideas.statement: Every Manifestation may truly be called the Seal of the Prophets and the First; the Beginning and the End are one reality.

ideas.title: The Manifestation's sovereignty is spiritual
ideas.statement: The sovereignty of the promised One is spiritual and inward — His ascendancy over hearts — not worldly dominion.

ideas.title: The revealed verses are the supreme testimony
ideas.statement: The Word of God — the revealed verses — is the greatest proof of a Manifestation, above all other signs and miracles.

ideas.title: The station of the Qá'im (the Báb)
ideas.statement: The promised Qá'im has appeared in the Báb, the Primal Point, whose Revelation fulfils and abrogates the former laws.

ideas.title: The twin testimonies: the Book and the Family
ideas.statement: The Book of God and the recognized expounders are the twin testimonies left by the Prophet for His people.

ideas.title: Each Revelation renews the law
ideas.statement: A new Manifestation annuls or changes the laws of the former Dispensation — prayer, fasting and ordinances — as a test for the people.

ideas.title: The Primal Will and the new creation
ideas.statement: Through the Primal Will the Manifestation brings a new creation; in every thing God's wisdom and signs are hidden.

ideas.title: The outpouring of divine grace through Revelation
ideas.statement: Divine grace and bounty flow to all creation through the Manifestations and never cease.

themes.title: The true seeker and the attainment of certitude

ideas.title: The conditions of the true seeker
ideas.statement: The true seeker must cleanse the heart of acquired learning and prejudice, rely on God alone, and search with the lamp of love and longing.

ideas.title: The purified heart as the mirror of truth
ideas.statement: Only a heart cleansed of worldly attachment and idle fancy can reflect the light of divine knowledge and recognize the truth.

ideas.title: Detachment from all save God
ideas.statement: Detachment from the world and from self is the condition for attaining the Presence of God and the mysteries of His Word.

ideas.title: Certitude (íqán)
ideas.statement: Certitude is the station in which the seeker, freed from doubt, sees with the eye of God; it is the aim of the book.

ideas.title: Divine knowledge versus human learning
ideas.statement: True knowledge is from God and bestowed on pure hearts; knowledge acquired by men, and 'satanic knowledge' born of self, veil from the truth.

ideas.title: The divine test and touchstone
ideas.statement: God tests the people with every Revelation, and the Manifestation is the touchstone that separates truth from falsehood.

ideas.title: Steadfastness, patience and resignation
ideas.statement: The believer must remain steadfast, patient and resigned to God's will amid trials, even unto sacrifice.

ideas.title: Sacrifice and martyrdom in the path of God
ideas.statement: Self-sacrifice and martyrdom in the path of God, as the companions of every Prophet showed, testify to the truth of the Cause.

ideas.title: The good-pleasure of God and the Riḍván
ideas.statement: The seeker's goal is the good-pleasure of God, the Riḍván of His nearness and reunion.

ideas.title: Faith as true life
ideas.statement: Faith is the true life; the one who believes is quickened by the Spirit, while the heedless are dead though living.

ideas.title: Equity in judgement
ideas.statement: The seeker must judge with equity and fairness, weighing the Revelation by its own proofs.

ideas.title: Guarding the tongue
ideas.statement: The seeker should shun idle talk and backbiting, for the fire of the tongue consumes the soul.

ideas.title: Forgiveness of sins
ideas.statement: The power to forgive sins belongs to God and is exercised through His chosen Ones.

ideas.title: True poverty and wealth
ideas.statement: True wealth is love of God and His chosen Ones; poverty is want of it, not want of possessions.
